S10.01.note: The side drawer's menu button has no visible label in the code I read.
steps: Open Projects (the Projects entry in the side drawer, which opens from the menu button).
Tap the floating "New project" button at the bottom right.
Type a name in the "Project name" field and tap "Create project".
Look for the new project in the Projects list, compared with Expected.
Open a chat.
Tap the "Conversation menu" button in the chat header.
Tap "Rename"; the "Rename chat" box opens with the field "Enter a new title".
Change the title and tap "Rename".
Look for the new title in the chat header, compared with Expected.

labels.text: Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats.

S10.05.needs: a Cloud account and a Cloud chat
S10.05.note: Archiving has no confirm step; it relies on the Undo message, which is different from Expected's first option only in that it does not ask first.
steps: Open a Cloud chat that is not temporary.
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Archive".
Note that no confirmation appears first; a message appears: "Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats." with an "Undo" button.
Go to Settings > Archived Chats and check the chat is there, compared with Expected.
Open a chat.
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Delete".
Read the "Delete chat?" dialog, which names the chat in quotes.
Tap "Cancel" to check nothing is removed, then repeat and tap "Delete", and compare with Expected.

S10.07.needs: a chat kept only on this device
S10.07.note: There is one Delete button and no second confirmation. Deleting a Cloud chat is not shown as permanent; the dialog says to restore it from Recently deleted on the web.
steps: Open a chat that is kept only on this device (not a Cloud chat).
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Delete".
Read the "Delete chat?" dialog: it says the chat is deleted from this device and cannot be restored.
Tap "Delete" and compare with Expected.
S10.07.where: Chat > Conversation menu > Delete (on a chat that is only on this device)

labels.text: Share a link to this chat?

S10.08.needs: a Cloud account and a saved chat
S10.08.note: For a temporary chat the menu shows "Share link" and first asks to save the chat.
steps: Open a saved Cloud chat (not a temporary chat).
Tap the "Conversation menu" button and tap "Share".
Read the dialog "Share a link to this chat?", which says anyone with the link can read the chat until it expires or you revoke it.
Tap "Create link"; the system share sheet opens with the link.
Compare with Expected: the link goes to the system share sheet, not a box in the app.
S10.08.where: Chat > Conversation menu > Share > Create link

S10.09.needs: an item in the Library and a device
S10.09.note: I found no link-creation option for files, only the system share sheet.
steps: Open Library from the side drawer.
Long-press a picture or file and tap "Share", or tap Select, pick one item and tap "Share" at the bottom.
Look for the system share sheet with that file.
Compare with Expected: the file goes to the system share sheet.

S10.10.needs: a Cloud account and an artifact that can be published
S10.10.note: The publish button's label is "Publish artifact to a public link" in the code (ArtifactFullScreen.tsx).
steps: On Chats, use the search field and type the artifact's title.
Under "Artifacts" in the results, tap the artifact.
Tap the globe button labelled "Publish artifact to a public link", then tap "Publish" in the dialog.
Under "Who can open this" choose "Anyone with the link", "Only people you invite" or "Everyone in this workspace", then compare with Expected.
Tap "Unpublish" and confirm "Unpublish this artifact?" to take it down.
S10.10.where: Chats search > Artifacts > open the artifact > Publish icon > Publish > Who can open this

S10.11.needs: a Cloud account and a previewable artifact
S10.11.note: In local mode the app says "Switch to AGI Cloud to publish" instead.
steps: Open a Cloud artifact that can be published (a page or app).
Tap the globe button "Publish artifact to a public link".
Read "Publish to a public link?" and tap "Publish".
Look for the published link and the "Copy publication link" button, and compare with Expected.
S10.11.where: Chats search > Artifacts > open the artifact > Publish artifact to a public link > Publish

S10.12.needs: a Cloud account with at least one shared link
S10.12.note: The screen offers Share and Revoke only; I found no control to change the expiry or the access of a link.
steps: Open Settings, then Privacy, then Chat privacy, then Shared links.
Read each row for its title and "Expires" date, or "This link has expired".
Tap "Revoke" on a row and read "Revoke this link?".
Tap "Revoke" to confirm and compare with Expected.
S10.12.where: Settings > Privacy > Chat privacy > Shared links

S10.13.needs: a Cloud workspace where the account can manage the team, and a second email address
S10.13.note: The administration section only shows when the account can manage the team.
steps: Open Settings, then Workspace.
Scroll to the administration section and tap "Invite by email".
Type an address in "Email address", pick a role (Member, Admin or Viewer), and tap "Send invitation".
Look at the pending invitations list; tap an invitation and choose "Resend invitation" or "Revoke invitation", and compare with Expected.

S10.14.needs: a Cloud workspace, an admin account, and a second member in the same workspace
S10.14.note: Ordinary role changes save without a separate confirmation; only an ownership transfer asks more.
steps: Open Settings, then Workspace, as an admin of the workspace.
On a member who is not you, tap "Change role".
In the sheet "Role for <name>", pick a role and tap "Save role".
Look at the member's role in the list, and compare with Expected.
S10.14.where: Settings > Workspace > Change role for <member name> > Change role

S10.17.needs: a Cloud chat and a file on the device
S10.17.note: The "File" card only appears in Cloud mode; "Photos" and "Camera" are the other upload cards.
steps: Open a Cloud chat and tap "Add to chat" next to the message box.
Tap "File"; the device file chooser opens.
Pick a file.
Look for the file attached to the message before sending, and compare with Expected.

S10.18.needs: a Cloud account and an account on the outside service
steps: Open Settings, then Connectors.
Tap a connector that is not connected yet.
Tap "Connect <name>"; for an OAuth service the browser opens the service's sign-in page, and for a key service the "Connect {connectorName}" sheet asks for the key.
Finish the authorization and return to the app, then look for the card showing "Connected", and compare with Expected.

S10.19.needs: a connection whose authorization has expired (hard to set up)
S10.19.note: I did not confirm in the code that the connector's settings are kept after reauthorizing; that is not verified.
steps: Open Settings, then Connectors, then the connector that shows "Authorization expired".
Tap "Reauthorize" and complete the authorization in the browser.
Return to the app and look for the connector showing as connected again, and compare with Expected.

S10.20.needs: several connected accounts for one service
S10.20.note: I searched apps/mobile for an account picker, a default account or several accounts for one connector (cloud-connectors and services/connectors.ts); the only match was "Reset ... to default" for tool permissions, so no picker was found.

labels.text: Chat is getting long. Start a fresh chat for faster responses.

S10.27.note: I did not check the length at which the warning appears.
steps: Open a long chat with many messages.
Look for the line "Chat is getting long. Start a fresh chat for faster responses." with a "New chat" button.
Tap "New chat" to start a fresh chat, or open the "Conversation menu" and tap "What is in context" to see the details, then compare with Expected.
S10.27.where: Chat > (a long conversation) > warning line under the header

S10.28.needs: a usage limit that has been reached
S10.28.note: The wording of the limit and the reset time come from server data; I did not find that text in the app code.
steps: Use a Free or other account until its usage limit is reached, then open a chat.
Look for the usage banner; if a reset time is known, tap "Notify me when it resets".
Tap the banner's action to open the recovery screen (Subscription), or tap "Dismiss usage warning".
Compare the banner's text (which limit, when it resets, what to do) with Expected.
S10.28.where: Chat > usage warning banner above the message box

S10.29.needs: a Cloud account; the purchase needs store products and in-app purchases switched on by the owner
S10.29.note: Partial: the section shows only when store products load; in-app billing is not finished (owner switch and waitlist), and the Expected purchase dialog from the limit screen was not found.
steps: Open Settings, then Subscription.
Look for the "Usage top-ups" section: "Credits add to your plan and don't expire."
Tap a credit amount to start a purchase, then compare with Expected.

S10.30.note: Partial: plan prices and the pick action depend on the billing flag and store products, which are not finished.
steps: Open Upgrade from the side drawer, or open Settings, then Subscription.
Tap "Compare plans" to see the plan list with prices and features.
Tap "Upgrade plan" or "Choose plan" if shown, and compare with Expected.
If the row shows "Unavailable in the app", plan changes are not available in the app.
S10.30.where: Settings > Subscription > Compare plans (or Upgrade, then Subscription)

S10.31.note: Partial: the app has no in-app cancel dialog; cancellation links out to the store or web billing.
steps: Open Settings, then Subscription.
Look at the "Access ends" or "Renews" row, and check the date shown.
Tap "Manage billing"; the web billing page opens in the browser (for a store subscription, a "Subscription managed elsewhere" dialog appears first).
Compare with Expected: cancellation is done on that page or in the store, not in the app.

S10.32.note: Partial: the card is not changed in the app; the app links to web billing.
steps: Open Settings, then Subscription.
Tap "Manage billing".
Look at the web billing page in the browser for the card on file, and compare with Expected.

S10.33.needs: a Cloud account and the way to confirm it is you
S10.33.note: I did not find a passkey option in the "Confirm it is you" dialog; the strategies are password, email code, authenticator code and backup code.
steps: Open Settings, then Account, then Email.
Tap "Delete Account" (a sensitive action).
Read the "Confirm it is you" dialog and enter a password, an email code, or an authenticator or backup code.
Look for the action continuing only after verification, and compare with Expected.

labels.text: Microphone access is off. Enable microphone permission in Settings to use voice.

S10.34.needs: a microphone and a way to deny the permission
S10.34.note: The system prompt text is in apps/mobile/app.config.js.
steps: Open a chat and tap "Start voice mode" (the accessibility label of the voice button).
On the system microphone prompt, read the text "AGI Mobile uses the microphone for voice input and real-time voice conversations with AI." then choose Don't Allow.
Tap voice again and read the "Voice input unavailable" alert with "Open Settings" or "Not now".
Compare with Expected; the message says microphone access is off and how to turn it on.
S10.34.where: Chat > Start voice mode (first use asks for the microphone)

S10.38.needs: a Cloud account and a request that triggers a tool approval (set by the server policy)
S10.38.note: I did not identify which tool triggers an approval; the trigger depends on server policy.
steps: Open a Cloud chat and ask for an action that a tool needs approval for.
Look for the tool row in the chat that shows the action and its decision buttons.
Tap "Allow once" or "Deny" for that call only, then compare with Expected.
For a broader scope such as "Allow for this chat" on a destructive tool, read the confirmation dialog first.
S10.38.where: Chat (Cloud) > a tool call that is awaiting approval > Allow once / Allow for this chat / Always allow / Deny

labels.text: Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI

S10.39.needs: a Cloud account with a connected outside tool; a chat that triggers a tool approval
S10.39.note: The notice is rendered by apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx; which tool actions trigger it is decided by the server, and the code does not show what destination text is listed on the card.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that runs in AGI Cloud.
Ask the agent for an action that uses a connected outside tool.
When the approval card appears, read the notice text and the destination it names.
Compare with Expected: the card should show what is being sent and let you allow or deny that one call.
S10.39.where: Chat screen > send a message that asks the agent to use a connected outside tool > the tool approval card that shows "Allow" and "Deny"

S10.40.needs: a desktop app paired on Managed Cloud (for a real test)
S10.40.note: Pairing exists in code but is hidden in this build: apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts sets companion to false, and apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/remote-control.tsx returns a feature-unavailable screen when the flag is off. The QR scanner is apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/QRScanner.tsx. Searched the settings and companion folders for a reachable entry point and found none while the flag is off.

S10.41.needs: a Free account or a Cloud account
S10.41.note: The schedule create screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/schedules/create.tsx) uses the same guard, but no visible entry label for it was found; the memory add button label was not found either.
steps: Open the Settings screen and go to the Assistant section, then tap Memory.
Tap the control that adds or edits a memory (the exact button label was not found in the code).
Type some text into the memory field without saving.
Close the sheet without saving, then compare with Expected: a "Discard changes?" alert should appear with "Discard" and "Keep Editing".
Repeat with a new schedule on the schedule create screen; the same guard is used there, but I could not find the screen's entry label.
S10.41.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory > add or edit memory sheet, then close it with unsaved text

S10.43.needs: a chat with at least one message
S10.43.note: The sheet also offers Print and Copy All Messages, and an empty chat shows "Nothing to Export" instead.
steps: Open any chat that has messages.
Tap the control labelled Conversation menu in the chat header.
Tap Export.
Tap Export as Markdown (or Export as PDF or Export as Text) and choose where to share the file.
Compare with Expected: the sheet should offer formats and the exported file should contain the conversation.
S10.43.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Export > sheet "Export Conversation" > Export as Markdown

S10.44.needs: a chat with an assistant answer
S10.44.note: The confirmation can also read "Saved on this device. Nothing was sent." when delivery is stored locally; the report sheet also appears on media in the Library viewer.
steps: Open a chat that has an answer from the assistant.
Tap Message actions on that answer (or long-press it) and tap Report….
Choose a category (for example Other) and optionally write a note.
Tap Send and compare the result with Expected: the confirmation should say the report was sent or saved on this device.
S10.44.where: Open a chat > on an assistant answer, tap Message actions > Report… > choose a category > Send

S10.45.note: The feedback screen is the route /(app)/feedback; the Settings entry point and its Support section were confirmed in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Support section, then tap Report App Issue.
Choose General Feedback (or the bug option) and type a message.
Tap Submit Feedback (or Email Feedback when the app sends by email).
Compare with Expected: the "Thank You!" alert should appear with "Your feedback has been submitted.".

S10.46.note: The consent is asked on every tap; no saved preference was found in the code.
steps: Open Settings, go to the Support section, and tap Export Diagnostics.
Read the alert "Share diagnostics?" and its text.
Tap Continue to share, or Cancel to stop.
Compare with Expected: the consent text should say what is sent, and nothing should be shared after Cancel.
S10.46.where: Settings > Support > Export Diagnostics > Share diagnostics? > Continue

S10.47.note: The export is shared through the system share sheet (shareCloudDataExport), not a download, and there is no request dialog before it runs; failure alerts are "Export failed" and "Export not saved".
steps: Sign in to an AGI Cloud account, open Settings, and go to the Account section.
Tap the Email row to open the cloud account screen.
Tap Export Cloud Data and wait for the share sheet.
Compare with Expected: the export should be delivered as a file to share or save. The code does not show a confirmation step first.
S10.47.where: Settings > Account > Email > Export Cloud Data

labels.text: Erasure is processed after the deadline and may take longer. Once erasure begins, it cannot be undone.

S10.48.needs: a throwaway signed-in AGI Cloud account (not a real one)
S10.48.note: The dialog text is built in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-account/deleteAccountConfirmation.ts, and the scheduled state can be cancelled from the same screen.
steps: Sign in to an AGI Cloud account, open Settings, tap the Email row in the Account section.
Scroll to Delete Account and tap it.
Read the "Delete Account" dialog text: it schedules deletion, names what is deleted, and says erasure cannot be undone once it begins.
Tap Delete Account to confirm, or Cancel to stop. Compare with Expected: the dialog should explain what is deleted and require this confirmation.
Use a throwaway test account only, because the deletion is scheduled for real.
S10.48.where: Settings > Account > Email > Delete Account > Delete Account
